title: fix(scripts): fold the platform checklist's forked line-citation grammar into the shared anchor core
body:
Fixes #18592

Clause-②: no — repo scripts only, nothing published moves.

The symbol-anchor half of `scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs` became a registered corpus at #18107. The **line-citation** half stayed forked: `SOURCE_LINE_CITATION`, `findSourceLineCitations` and a family-file loop of its own, beside the shared sweep that already ran in the same file. Two graders for one rule, and they had drifted in **both** directions.

The direction is the 2026-09-01 director ruling written in `scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs`'s own header, verbatim: 「⛔ Do not fork this file for a second corpus; if a corpus needs behaviour this core lacks, **widen the core**」and「Two copies of that rule drift, and they drift **SILENTLY**」. So the core was widened and the fork deleted. ⛔ The other direction — patching both grammars into agreement — is what that ruling forbids.

## Readings, taken on this branch's own base (`a7bafc29af`), not copied

```
grep -c , scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs     BEFORE      AFTER
  SOURCE_LINE_CITATION                                  6          2   ← both survivors are MENTIONS:
  findSourceLineCitations                               3          2     the history note and the
  LINE_ANCHOR                                           0          1     anti-re-fork pin that names them
  pathlessLineCitations                                 0          7

grep -c , scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs               BEFORE      AFTER
  LINE_ANCHOR                                           3          3
  SOURCE_LINE_CITATION / findSourceLineCitations        0          0
  pathlessLineCitations                                 0         13

CONTROL, same read, same two files: symbolResolutionClass = 3 / 18 before AND after
⇒ both non-zero, so the zeros above are readings.
```

## Q1 — which spellings must the widened core recognise? BOTH difference sets, printed

Enumerated mechanically: the fork's regex literal was **extracted from source**, never retyped, and driven against the shared extractor over 62 probes (both self-test batteries, the nine spellings the shared `LINE_SPEC` docblock names, and the union of the two extension vocabularies).

**Direction A — the fork recognised, the shared core did not** (5 spelling classes):

| spelling | example |
|---|---|
| bare colon continuation | `ManifestSchema id :140 and version :202` |
| parenthesised bare form | `holds ONLY auditor (:395)` |
| the `~:` approximation | `computeAuthGate ~:5084-5160` |
| the `L` line pin | `registerRecordShareEndpoints ~L7246-7331` |
| the `html` extension | a citation into a template page |

**Direction B — the shared core recognised, the fork did not** (2 classes):

| spelling | example |
|---|---|
| tilde bare-number form | a tilde before a backticked number |
| comma continuation span | a backticked comma-then-line-spec |
| five extensions | `go`, `jsx`, `prisma`, `rs`, `scss` |

Direction B was already reaching this corpus through the registered sweep; it is the fork's own detector that was blind to it. Deleting the fork ends the disagreement from that side too.

## How far the core was widened, and why not further

Three edits, and the third one's **default is a measurement, not caution**:

1. `html` joins `ANCHORABLE_EXTENSIONS` — the shared vocabulary, which this gate's own header already prescribed as the exit ("widen the shared vocabulary … ⛔ never re-fork a private extension set here"). Measured additive: **zero** `.html` tokens read as an anchor or a citation across all five registered corpora.
2. The approximation tilde inside the colon form is admitted into `LINE_ANCHOR` for **every** corpus. Measured: **one** occurrence tree-wide, in the fork's own documentation of the spelling.
3. The two **path-less** spellings become a third corpus declaration, `pathlessLineCitations`, **defaulted OFF** — the same shape `unspannedAnchors` and `excludeDirs` took at #18107. Turned on corpus-wide they would fire **222** (bare colon) and **23** (`L` pin) times across `docs/adr/**`, `scripts/**` and `packages/spec/src/**` — `(:3000)` dev-server ports, `L11`/`L12`/`L13` scenario labels, docblock back-references — essentially all false positives, because in prose a colon before digits is punctuation. In this checklist's **data**, beside the filename it continues, it is a line pin. ⛔ And no whitespace is admitted after the colon: `**Date**: 2026-04-19` fires 26 times in `docs/adr/**` alone if it is.

## Q2 — does folding it in turn the gate red? **No. Measured before the edit.**

BEFORE, on `a7bafc29af`: `pnpm check:platform-checklist` exit **0**, `source citations: 20 family files carry no file:line pin`. The candidate patterns applied to the live 20-document family: bare colon **0**, `L` pin **0**, colon-tilde **0**, `.html` citation **0**, `.html` anchor **0**.

AFTER: exit **0**, `line citations: 0 survive across 20 swept documents`. ⛔ **No checklist data was edited** — none needed to be, and none was.

The symbol-anchor numbers beside it are unmoved: `577/633 resolved, 56 on the named #16898 residual, 17 file floors held, 20 swept documents` — identical before and after.

## Acceptance controls

Both run side-by-side against a second worktree pinned at `a7bafc29af`, so BEFORE is a real tree and not a recollection. Full output in the report on the card.

**LIT — direction A** (`silent -> JUDGED`, seven rows, every one flipped):

```
bare colon continuation      before=[]  after=[":140",":202"]
parenthesised bare citation  before=[]  after=[":395"]
`~:` approximation           before=[]  after=[":5084-5160"]
`~L` line pin                before=[]  after=["~L7246-7331"]
bare `L` line pin            before=[]  after=["L7477-7493"]
tilde INSIDE the colon form  before=[]  after=["packages/ui/AiChatPage.tsx:~605-615"]
`.html` line citation        before=[]  after=["examples/app/public/index.html:42"]
```

**LIT — direction B**, driven against the fork's own extracted regex, which is silent on all four while the widened core judges them:

```
tilde backticked number   fork=[] -> shared AFTER fires
comma continuation span   fork=[] -> shared AFTER fires
`.go` line citation       fork=[] -> shared AFTER fires
`.scss` line citation     fork=[] -> shared AFTER fires
CONTROL for the fork predicate (it must be capable of firing): [".ts:1276-1331"]
```

**DARK — verdicts both graders already agreed on, unchanged.** Six judged spellings (file-anchored, hyphen range, en-dash range, comma/slash list, open-ended plus, backticked continuation) stay `JUDGED -> JUDGED`; nine colon-then-digit neighbours (HTTP status, config literal, URL port, clock time, quoted JSON, capital-L identifier, i18n token, one-digit `L`, colon-then-space) stay `silent -> silent`. And with the declaration OFF — every other corpus — five probes read **byte-identical** before and after.

One honest nuance inside the DARK set: on a line carrying **both** a path-anchored citation and a trailing bare one, the bare one is now caught too. The agreed spelling keeps its verdict; the extra hit is the fold working, and the fork caught it as well.

## Verification

- `node scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs --self-test` — 149 cases (122 → 149; the fork's 19 spelling cases transplanted, firing rows and silent neighbours alike).
- `pnpm check:platform-checklist` — exit 0; its battery 19 → 9, reshaped from a grammar to a **binding**: the corpus declaration, a source read finding no citation regex here, its control, the binding driven ON and OFF against one text, the DARK case, the over-firing refusal, and the live zero with its control.
- All five other corpus gates green, verdict lines **identical** before/after for `docs/adr/**` and `packages/spec/src/**`. `scripts/**` moves only by my own comment prose (3500 → 3501 anchors); its line-anchor count stays 0 and its declined count stays **15**.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 31 families; all 31 run, `--ran` reconciliation: **31 derived, 31 run, 0 UNRUN**.
- `eslint . --no-inline-config` over eslint's own population — **6843 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings**, at `88172978c7`.

## Changeset — measured, not inferred from the path

`skip-changeset`. 70 packages declare a `files[]`; **0** entries cover either edited file, under a predicate whose positive control (`packages/spec` → `dist/index.js`) resolves. The root package is `private`. A tree-wide grep for the new symbols outside `scripts/` returns **0** files, with a live positive control returning 533. Nothing published moves.

## Acceptance notes

- `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` carries one row: `COMPOUND_ANCHOR_LEDGER` requires every compound self-test name to be classified in the same edit that introduces it, so the renamed battery's row moves with it. Same classification, same totals.
- Noted, not filed: adding `html` to the shared vocabulary extends — it does not open — the class where an external URL ending in a path-shaped fragment is read as an anchor by a corpus declaring `unspannedAnchors`. `.md` and `.json` URLs already sat in that class. Measured today: one such token exists tree-wide, in a `packages/spec` docblock, and that corpus does not declare `unspannedAnchors`, so it is unreachable. Carrier named: whoever next widens `UNSPANNED_ANCHOR`'s left boundary.
